subsystems.name: Heat source
subsystems.role: provides the thermal power to melt a descending borehole through the ice.
parts: radioisotope heat unit (e.g. plutonium-238) or small fission reactor

subsystems.name: Melting probe body
subsystems.role: the descending vehicle that transfers heat to the ice and houses all systems.

subsystems.name: Tether and power/data link
subsystems.role: supplies power from the surface and returns data and samples.
parts: reinforced cable with copper power lines and fibre-optic data lines

subsystems.name: Navigation and control
subsystems.role: steers the probe and manages descent through unknown ice layers.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: analyses meltwater and ocean water for signs of habitability.

subsystems.name: Hybrid cutting head
subsystems.role: handles debris or ice lenses that pure melting cannot penetrate.

buildSteps.title: Design the probe
buildSteps.detail: Thermal and structural models balance heat loss against melting rate, set the descent speed, and choose materials that survive extreme cold and pressure.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the hull
buildSteps.detail: A pressure-resistant, insulated body is built with a heated nose cone and channels to spread heat evenly into the ice.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the heat source
buildSteps.detail: The radioisotope or reactor unit is assembled and tested to deliver continuous thermal power for months or years.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture the tether
buildSteps.detail: A long reinforced cable with power and data lines is produced and wound onto a spool, then tested under tension and at cryogenic temperatures.

buildSteps.title: Assemble control and science systems
buildSteps.detail: Radar, sonar, computers, and instruments for sampling and analysing meltwater are installed and wired to the tether.

buildSteps.title: Bench and cold-chamber testing
buildSteps.detail: The complete probe operates in a cold chamber and melts through large ice blocks to verify energy balance and communication.

buildSteps.title: Field test in a terrestrial glacier
buildSteps.detail: The cryobot is deployed in a glacier to melt hundreds of metres down, validating descent, tether handling, and data return.

buildSteps.title: Space-qualify and deploy
buildSteps.detail: The probe is subjected to launch vibrations and vacuum, then landed on an icy moon to begin its descent to the ocean.

prerequisites.why: decades of spacecraft use prove they can supply heat and electricity for years in deep space.
tested on the ground but not flown for decades; they offer far more power for fast melting.
radar and sensors exist, but full autonomy for kilometre-scale descent through unknown ice is unproven.
cables exist, but operation in ice for months without breaking or shorting is not demonstrated.
sterilisation protocols and clean assembly can prevent contaminating an alien ocean with Earth microbes.
missions like Europa Clipper and JUICE will map ice thickness and ocean depth, telling engineers where to land and how deep to melt.

pathway.milestone: prototype cryobots tested in glaciers, descending tens to hundreds of metres
pathway.unlocks: basic melting, tether, and communication technology.

pathway.milestone: full-scale cryobot tested in Antarctic ice to reach a subglacial lake
pathway.unlocks: proof of kilometre-scale descent and long-term tether operation.

pathway.milestone: a cryobot mission to Europa or Enceladus, guided by Europa Clipper and JUICE data
pathway.unlocks: direct sampling of a subsurface ocean for habitability.

pathway.milestone: routine access to subsurface oceans, possibly with autonomous submersibles
pathway.unlocks: extensive exploration and life-detection in alien seas.
